name: Nuclear risk
value: No US–Russia limits; N Korea tests surge
summary: New START has lapsed without replacement; North Korean weapons tests surge; no nuclear test or alert change found
state: New START has expired, and the US rejected Russia's offer to keep observing its central limits while seeking a new treaty (Arms Control Association, 1 Nov). Bloomberg reported on 8 Nov that North Korean weapons tests are running at twice the pace of Trump's first term. Zaporizhzhia lost all off-site power on 8 Nov before it was restored (Moscow Times). Searches on 10 Nov found no nuclear test, alert-level change or explicit threat of use.
for_you: No change in practical risk for the public. UK guidance on radiation emergencies is published by UKHSA.
rubric_hit: Arms-control lapse without replacement (New START); no test or alert-level change

sources.title: Arms Control Association — Nuclear-weapon states consult as Trump talks denuclearization
Bloomberg — North Korea's weapons tests surge to twice Trump first-term pace
The Moscow Times — Zaporizhzhia nuclear plant relying on generators again

why: Nuclear use anywhere would be a civilisational shock; arms-control treaties are weaker than at any time since the 1960s.
drivers: Threats in active wars, testing, doctrine changes, arms-control collapse, proliferation.

rubric.alert: A nuclear test, changes in deployment/alert levels, or threatened use in an active conflict.
rubric.watch: Explicit threats, unusual exercises, doctrine changes, or arms-control lapses without replacement.
rubric.normal: No explicit nuclear threats or tests; arms-control dialogue active.
